target.title: fix(commitments): reject calendar-invalid due timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where inferred commitments could accept an impossible calendar date from model output. For example, `2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z` was normalized into May and could persist a check-in for a date the model never validly expressed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Due timestamps now use the existing strict absolute-time validation before retaining the original `Date.parse` result, preserving current timezone behavior. An invalid optional latest bound continues to use the existing 12-hour fallback instead of being normalized into another month.

This PR was AI-assisted. I reviewed the resulting code and tests and ran the repository's structured Codex autoreview.

Risk note: the change adds a single guard clause (`parseAbsoluteTimeMs(raw) !== null`) to an existing local helper `parseDueMs` in `src/commitments/extraction.ts:256`, reusing an established strict parser (`src/cron/parse.ts:65`) that shipped in v2026.6.9. The blast radius is limited to the inferred-commitment extraction pipeline; valid ISO timestamps, leap days, and explicit timezone offsets are preserved in the regression tests.

## User Impact

Users will no longer receive inferred commitment check-ins scheduled from calendar-invalid model timestamps. Valid leap-day and explicit timezone-offset timestamps continue to work as before.

## Evidence

### Negative control — pre-fix gate accepts impossible calendar dates (real source functions)

`node --import tsx` drove the real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` from `src/cron/parse.ts` against the pre-fix `parseDueMs` logic (Date.parse only):

```
Input: 2026-04-31T17:00:00.000Z
Date.parse result: 1777654800000 (finite: true)
Date.parse builds: 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
parseAbsoluteTimeMs: null

Pre-fix gate:  Number.isFinite(parsed) only → ACCEPTED (BUG — normalized to May 1)
Post-fix gate: Number.isFinite(parsed) && parseAbsoluteTimeMs !== null → REJECTED (FIXED)
```

### Real-behavior proof — after fix (real `parseAbsoluteTimeMs` + new `parseDueMs` logic)

Full proof harness exercising the real `src/cron/parse.ts` strict parser at `node --import tsx`:

```
========================================================================
  REAL-BEHAVIOR PROOF — PR #106236
  fix(commitments): reject calendar-invalid due timestamps
========================================================================

PART 1 — parseAbsoluteTimeMs (the strict guard) raw output
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       parseAbsoluteTimeMs → null (REJECTED)
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       parseAbsoluteTimeMs → null (REJECTED)
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2025-03-01T10:00:00.000Z
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1835438400000
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1784106000…
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             parseAbsoluteTimeMs → 1784106000…
   JS Date.parse builds:                 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z

PART 2 — BEFORE fix (old parseDueMs = Date.parse only)
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       ACCEPTED → 2026-05-01T17:00:00.000Z
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       ACCEPTED → 2025-03-01T10:00:00.000Z
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   ACCEPTED → 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  OLD totals: 5 accepted, 1 rejected

PART 3 — AFTER fix (new parseDueMs = Date.parse + strict parse)
  [invalid calendar date (Apr 31)]       REJECTED (undefined)
  [invalid calendar date (Feb 29)]       REJECTED (undefined)
  [valid leap day (Feb 29, leap year)]   ACCEPTED → 2028-02-29T12:00:00.000Z
  [valid normal date]                    ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [valid date +08:00 offset]             ACCEPTED → 2026-07-15T09:00:00.000Z
  [undefined input]                      REJECTED (undefined)

  NEW totals: 3 accepted, 3 rejected

VERDICT
  Apr 31 rejected BEFORE fix: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to May 1)
  Apr 31 rejected AFTER  fix: YES ✓
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected BEFORE: NO ← BUG (Date.parse normalizes to Mar 1)
  Feb 29 (non-leap) rejected AFTER : YES ✓
  Valid leap day still accepted: YES ✓
  Valid normal date still accepted: YES ✓

  → FIX WORKS: invalid calendar dates blocked, valid dates preserved.
```

### Automated tests

- Focused test file passes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commitments/extraction.test.ts` — 1 file, 8 tests all green.
- Negative control: pre-fix test assertion confirmed the invalid-date test fails without the guard.

### Formatting / static checks

- `oxfmt src/commitments/extraction.ts src/commitments/extraction.test.ts` — clean.
- `git diff --check` — clean.
- Structured autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings.

### What was not tested

The full build, check, and test suites require a CI environment; those gates are covered by the fork PR CI run. Live provider/gateway commitment extraction end-to-end was not tested locally because it requires a configured model provider and session state that was not available in the contributor checkout. The evidence above exercises the exact changed code path (`parseDueMs` + `parseAbsoluteTimeMs`) with real source functions from the tree.
